method_html:
Delivery method for governed automation

How to take a repetitive operations process from the first stakeholder call to a robot that runs in production, passes audit, and fails safely. There are seven stages. Each stage ends with a gate: a named person signs a named artefact before the next stage starts. The toolbox supplies the building blocks for every design decision, so robots look and fail the same way.

This page is a method, not your bank's policy. Where your bank has its own standard (technology risk, change management, data classification, end-user computing, outsourcing), that standard wins. Use the artefacts here as the evidence it asks for.

Principles

  1. Deterministic. The same input gives the same output. Every decision the robot makes is a written rule with an owner. No hidden judgement in code.
  2. Fail loud, never silently wrong. A value the robot cannot read becomes blank and an exception. It is never guessed.
  3. Every item ends in exactly one state: done, exception with a reason, or retry later. Nothing disappears.
  4. Nothing irreversible happens twice or without four eyes. Submits, payments and emails are checked before every retry. Money movements and customer-facing actions go through maker-checker.
  5. Least privilege. The robot uses a service account with only the access the process needs. Secrets live in a vault, never in code or config.
  6. Evidence by default. Every run keeps what came in, what went out, control totals, who approved, and which version and rules ran.
  7. The business owns the rules. Thresholds, mappings and routing live in a rules sheet or config the process owner signs off. The robot applies them.
  8. There is always a manual fallback, and the team has rehearsed it.

The seven stages

# Stage Goal You produce Gate: who signs Toolbox
1 Intake and triage Decide if this is worth automating, and how much Intake record, suitability score Your lead / automation CoE
2 Discovery Understand the process exactly as it runs today Process definition (PDD), samples Process owner describe_shape, synth
3 Design Decide how the robot does each step and how it fails Solution design (SDD), exception table, controls Peer review; risk / controls where required patterns, RETRY_PROFILES
4 Build Build from tested blocks, the same way every time Robot code, config, rules sheet, unit tests Code review template, patterns, recipes
5 Test Prove it on every edge case and in UAT Test evidence, UAT sign-off Process owner --dry-run, synth
6 Deploy Release through change control Change record, runbook, access approvals Change approver schtasks_create, single_instance
7 Run and improve Monitor, handle exceptions, keep it current, retire it cleanly KPIs, incident log, periodic review Process owner, yearly exit codes, logs, evidence pack

1. Intake and triage

Score the request before you book a long call. Score each line 0, 1 or 2.

Question 0 1 2
Are the decisions rules, not judgement? Mostly judgement Some judgement All rules
Are the inputs digital and structured? Paper / free text Mixed Files, tables, systems
Are the systems and screens stable? Change monthly Change yearly Stable or API
Volume A few a month Daily Many per day, or peaks
Cost of an error today Low Medium High (money, customer, regulatory)
Time it takes people today < 2 h / month 2–20 h / month > 20 h / month
Exceptions Most items Some Few
  • 10 or more: automate end to end (unattended).
  • 6 to 9: automate the preparation and checks, keep a human for the decisions (attended, or maker-checker).
  • Under 6: fix the process or the data first. A robot would copy the mess faster.

Rough benefit: hours saved per month = items per month × minutes per item ÷ 60 × (1 − exception rate). Put the error-cost reduction next to it. In a bank it is often worth more than the hours.

2. Discovery: the stakeholder call

Before the call ask for: the procedure document if one exists, a screen recording of one normal item and one awkward item, two or three masked sample inputs and outputs, the list of systems and who grants access. Run describe_shape(df) on a sample to see column patterns without seeing values. That output is safe to share and to paste into an AI tool.

On the call walk through a real item live, click by click. Ask "what do you do if…" at every step. Use these questions:

  • Outcome. What is the result, who uses it, and what happens if it is late or wrong?
  • Trigger and timing. What starts the work? When? Which cut-offs, time zones and holiday calendars apply? What happens at month end?
  • Inputs. Where does each input come from, in what format, at what time? How often is it late, incomplete or laid out differently? Do the headers change?
  • Steps and rules. Which decisions are made, on what rule, written down where? Who owns each rule?
  • Systems and access. Which applications, which versions? Is it Citrix? Is there MFA? Can a service account be used? Is there an API or an export instead of screens?
  • Outputs and handover. What is produced, where is it stored, who is told?
  • Exceptions. What are the five things that go wrong most often? What do you do for each one? How often does each happen?
  • Controls. What do you check today: totals, reconciliations, a second pair of eyes, sign-offs? What would an auditor ask for?
  • Data. Is there customer or personal data? What is its classification? Who may see it?
  • Volumes. Items per day, the peak, the month-end spike, the longest single item.
  • Fallback. If the robot is down, who does the work by hand, and how fast must it be done?
  • Change. How often do screens, files or rules change, and who tells you?

Listen for these phrases. Each one changes the design:

They say It means Design response
"We usually just…" An unwritten rule Write it down, give it an owner, put it in the rules sheet
"Sometimes the file is late" Trigger and timeout wait_for_file with a deadline, then hand over to a human
"We check it against…" A control control_totals, reconcile
"Only Jane knows how" Key-person risk Document the rule before you build
"We fix it by hand" An exception path BusinessError code plus an exceptions report
"It depends on the client" A decision table first_match with the table in Excel
"The screen sometimes freezes" Retry and fallback attempt with RETRY_PROFILES['ui']

Capture the process in one table, one row per step:

# Actor System Action Input Output Rule / decision Exceptions Control Volume / time
1 Ops Outlook Save the attachment from the custodian mail Mail .xlsx Sender is custodian X No mail by 09:00 – 1 / day

After the call send the table and a one-page summary back within two days and ask the process owner to confirm it. Gate: the process owner signs the process definition (PDD).

3. Design

Design each step, then design how each step fails. Write both into the solution design (SDD).

Choose the route for each step, best first:

  1. Remove the step: does anyone use its output?
  2. Data or API: an official API, a database view, or the JSON the portal page itself calls (api_over_ui pattern).
  3. A file export the system already produces.
  4. The screen: desktop (pywinauto), web (Browser), Citrix (pyautogui images). Use it only when nothing above exists.

Map each step to a block. Every row of the process table should name the toolbox function or pattern it uses. If nothing fits, design a new block and add it to the toolbox, instead of hand-coding it in one robot.

Exception design. Every failure has a kind, an action and an audience:

Failure Kind Robot does Who is told Block
Account not found, amount mismatch Business (data is wrong) Record it, skip the item, carry on Process owner, in the exceptions report BusinessError, process_all
File locked, screen slow, network blip System (environment) Retry per profile, then stop after 3 in a row Support, by exit code 3 attempt, process_all
Login refused, password expired Access Stop at once, never retry Owner and support RobotError AUTH, login_once
A bug (TypeError, AttributeError) Bug Stop at once Developer, exit code 5 classify
Input missing or broken Input Stop before processing Process owner, exit code 2 safe_input
Past the cut-off Timing Do not submit; hand over Process owner assert_before_cutoff

Retry policy. Use the named profiles in RETRY_PROFILES and change them only in one place:

Profile Tries Wait Check up to Why
ui 3 2 s 10 s Screens lag and pop-ups steal focus; still fails within about a minute
page_load 2 5 s 60 s Slow searches and reports; one reload is enough
file_lock 5 10 s, doubling – Someone has the file open in Excel
read 3 2 s, doubling – API GET, query, download: safe to repeat
submit 1 – 30 s Post, pay, send: more tries only with an already_done check
login 1 – 30 s A repeated wrong password locks the service account

On top of the profiles: after a step gives up, the item loop stops after 3 system failures in a row, so a dead system is not hammered for every item.

Controls.

  • Input control totals (rows, sum, absolute sum, distinct keys) are recorded before processing and reconciled after.
  • An output reconciliation runs against the source or the target system.
  • Maker-checker applies to anything irreversible or customer-facing. The checker is a named person, never the robot's account.
  • Segregation of duties: the developer does not approve production changes or hold production credentials.
  • Every run keeps an evidence pack: inputs and outputs with hashes, totals, approvals, rule file version, log.

Data protection. Classify the data. Logs carry ids, never values (get_logger redacts). Screenshots stay in the run folder under the retention rule. Test with synthetic data (synth). Share shapes, not values (describe_shape).

Access. Use a service account per robot, with least privilege. Credentials come from the vault (get_secret). Plan MFA with the security team early, since it decides whether a step can be unattended.

Run design. Choose the trigger: schedule, file arrival, mail or webhook. Add a single-instance lock, business-day and cut-off guards, a run folder per business date, and exit codes that monitoring understands. Choose attended or unattended.

Fallback. The manual procedure stays current. The robot has a kill switch (a STOP file) and a dry-run mode.

Solution design (SDD) outline: purpose and scope, process (to-be) with the route per step, inputs and outputs, rules and owners, exception table, retry policy, controls, data classification and protection, access and credentials, schedule and triggers, evidence and retention, monitoring and exit codes, fallback and kill switch, open risks. Gate: peer review, plus risk or controls review where your policy requires it.

4. Build

  • Start from templates/robot_template.py. It gives you --env, --dry-run, --business-date, a lock, a run folder, JSON logs, a checkpoint and exit codes.
  • Build steps from patterns (copy the block, keep its decisions). Build data flows from recipes (a YAML spec validated against the real functions, which can generate the script).
  • Keep one config per environment. Secrets never go in config. Rules live in a sheet the business owns.
  • Make every step safe to re-run: business keys, not row numbers; checkpoints; already_done before any repeat of a submit.
  • Test with synthetic data first.

Code review checklist:

  • Every failure path raises the right kind: BusinessError, SystemError_, or a stop.
  • Nothing sends, pays or submits without dry-run support and a double-send guard.
  • No secrets, no data in logs, no personal accounts.
  • Control totals are reconciled in and out.
  • Edge cases from the test checklist are covered by tests.
  • The version and the rules file hash are recorded in the evidence.

Gate: code review by a second engineer.

5. Test

Data edge cases that every robot is tested against:

  • Upper / lower / mixed case, leading and trailing spaces, non-breaking spaces, tabs.
  • Blanks, NA, -, zero; duplicate keys; zero-padded ids (00123 vs 123).
  • Number formats: (1,000), 1,000-, 1,000 DR, 1.234,56, currency symbols and codes.
  • Date formats: day-first, ISO, Excel serials, 20260306, 9999-12-31, dates without a year.
  • An empty file, missing or renamed columns, extra columns, a very large file, non-Latin names.

Environment edge cases:

  • A late, missing or locked file; an application that is down, slow or shows a pop-up.
  • An expired session or password; a network timeout after a submit.
  • A run after the cut-off or on a holiday; a second copy started by the scheduler.
  • A crash mid-run, then a re-run: it must resume, and nothing may be sent twice.

Levels:

  1. Unit tests with synthetic data (pytest).
  2. System test in the test environment, first with --dry-run, then live.
  3. UAT on masked real samples. The process owner checks the outputs and the exceptions report.
  4. Parallel run: the robot and the team process the same days, typically 5 to 10 business days. Compare the results until they match.

Gate: the process owner signs UAT, with the test evidence attached.

6. Deploy

The change record carries the robot version, the SDD, the test evidence, the runbook, access approvals, the schedule, and a rollback plan (disable the schedule, run by hand). Hypercare runs for the first two weeks: the developer checks every run.

Runbook (one page): what the robot does and when; inputs and where they come from; outputs and who receives them; the exit code table and what to do for each code; how to re-run for a business date; how to stop it (the kill switch); the manual fallback; contacts.

Exit Meaning Action
0 OK None
2 Business exceptions, or input rejected Owner works the exceptions report; if no report, read run.log.jsonl
3 System failure Re-run later; the checkpoint resumes
4 Config error Support fixes the config
5 Robot error Developer fixes; run by hand meanwhile
6 Already running None, or check for a stuck run

Gate: the change approver signs the change record.

7. Run, monitor, improve, retire

  • Monitor exit codes and exception counts after every run. Repeated exit 3 means the environment needs a fix, not more retries.
  • KPIs per month: items processed, straight-through rate, exceptions by code, run time, failed runs, hours saved.
  • Exceptions SLA: the owner works the report the same day.
  • Change triggers: a screen, file layout or rule change sends the robot back to stage 3. Rule changes in the rules sheet need the owner's sign-off and show up in the evidence through the file hash.
  • Periodic review, at least yearly: confirm access, rules, owner, fallback and that the robot is still needed.
  • Retire cleanly: remove the schedule, revoke the service account, archive the evidence under the retention rule, and update the procedure.

Artefacts at a glance

Artefact Stage Written by Approved by Toolbox help
Intake record and score 1 You Lead / CoE Section 1 table
Process definition (PDD) 2 You Process owner Capture table, describe_shape
Solution design (SDD) 3 You Peer; risk / controls Exception and retry tables, patterns
Rules sheet 3–4 Process owner Process owner rules_from_excel, business_rules pattern
Code, config, tests 4 You Code reviewer Template, patterns, recipes, synth
Test evidence, UAT sign-off 5 You, owner Process owner --dry-run, evidence pack
Change record, runbook 6 You Change approver Exit code table, schtasks_create
Run evidence Every run The robot Kept per retention controls_evidence, get_logger
Periodic review 7 You, owner Process owner KPIs from logs

BusinessError (data is wrong) -> recorded with retryable False and skipped; SystemError_ / OSError

decisions: Check the result on the screen, not the click: a click that 'worked' but saved nothing is the failure that matters.
3 tries 2 s apart, each checked for up to 10 s (RETRY_PROFILES['ui']): covers a slow screen and one pop-up, and still fails within about a minute.
Between tries press Esc and re-focus the window (recover), so one stray dialog does not spoil every retry.
One fallback route (the keyboard shortcut instead of the button): a different way in beats repeating the same one.
On giving up: screenshot as evidence, then SystemError_ STEP_FAILED. process_all stops after 3 such failures in a row and the template exits 3 (re-run later).
governance: already_done checks the record before every try, so a slow save is never posted twice.
Screenshots can show customer data: keep them in the run folder, under your data retention rule, never in a shared drive.
The log line for each failed try names the step and the reference only, never field values.

def quietly(close, what, log):
    """Run one closer; a failure is logged by name and swallowed, so it never replaces the error being handled."""
    try:
        close()
    except Exception as e:
        log.warning(f"close {what} failed", extra={"code": "CLOSE_FAILED", "type": type(e).__name__})


def enter(stack, cm, what, log):
    """stack.enter_context for an app, with its close run through quietly(); the app cannot swallow the error."""
    value = cm.__enter__()
    stack.push(lambda et, e, tb: quietly(lambda: cm.__exit__(et, e, tb), what, log))
    return value


def on_error(take, log):
    """Exit hook for stack.push: take() evidence on an error only, while the screens are still open."""
    return lambda et, e, tb: e is not None and quietly(take, "evidence", log)      # falsy: the error goes on


def open_apps(stack, rd, log):
    """Open each app and register its closer at once: whatever fails later, they close in reverse order."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%H%M%S")                                        # per run: a re-run keeps old evidence
    b = enter(stack, Browser(rd / "screenshots" / stamp), "browser", log)  # screenshots itself on an error exit
    xl = enter(stack, excel_app(), "excel", log)                           # its own EXCEL.EXE, always quit
    app = app_connect(exe=r"C:\Apps\Core\core.exe")                        # started by the robot, so ours to kill
    stack.callback(quietly, app.kill, "core app", log)
    stack.push(on_error(lambda: screen_capture(rd / f"failed_screen_{stamp}.png"), log))   # first out: app open
    return b, xl, app


def check_stop(rd, cfg=None):
    """Kill switch: SystemError_ STOPPED if ops put a STOP file in the run folder or switched robot_enabled off."""
    if any((rd / n).exists() for n in ("STOP", "STOP.txt")) or not feature_flag("robot_enabled", cfg, default=True):
        raise SystemError_("stopped by the kill switch", code="STOPPED")


def until_stop(items, rd, cfg=None):
    """Yield items, checking the kill switch before each one: a stop lands between two items, never inside one."""
    for item in items:
        check_stop(rd, cfg)
        yield item


def exit_code(exc):
    """Template exit codes: a second copy 6, BusinessError 2, retryable 3, anything else 5."""
    err = classify(exc)
    return 6 if err.code == "ALREADY_RUNNING" else 2 if isinstance(err, BusinessError) else 3 if err.retryable else 5


def notify_owner(facts, log, dry_run=False, post=None):
    """Status-only Teams card, sent once; a failed send is logged and the exit code stands."""
    try:
        url = "" if dry_run else get_secret("TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL")
        return teams_message(url, f"{ROBOT}: {facts['Status']}", facts, color="D13438", dry_run=dry_run, post=post)
    except Exception as e:
        log.warning("notify failed", extra={"code": "NOTIFY_FAILED", "type": type(e).__name__})


def run_robot(rd, items, handle, report, log, cfg=None, cp=None, key=str, opener=open_apps, notify=notify_owner,
              dry_run=False):
    """In the template's run() after SETUP; drop main()'s single_instance block: one ExitStack, a card -> exit code."""
    try:
        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
            stack.enter_context(single_instance(ROBOT, lock_dir=rd))         # first in, so released last
            check_stop(rd, cfg)                                              # before any app opens
            apps = opener(stack, rd, log)
            done, failures = process_all(until_stop(items, rd, cfg), lambda item: handle(apps, item),
                                         checkpoint=cp, key=key)             # no log=: it repeats messages
            report(done, failures)                                           # every item failure, on file
        code = 3 if failures["retryable"].any() else 2 if len(failures) else 0
        facts = {"Error code": "", "Done": len(done), "Exceptions": len(failures)}
    except Exception as e:
        info, code = error_info(e), exit_code(e)
        ctx = {k: v for k, v in info["context"].items() if k != "history"}   # ids only: history repeats messages
        level = log.warning if info["code"] in ("ALREADY_RUNNING", "STOPPED") else log.error
        level(f"run ended early [{info['code']}]", extra={"code": info["code"], "type": type(e.__cause__ or e).__name__,
              "where": ctx.pop("where", info["where"]), "context": ctx})    # type: the bug, not process_all's wrapper
        facts = {"Error code": info["code"]}
    if code not in (0, 6):                                                   # apps closed, lock released
        status = "STOPPED" if facts["Error code"] == "STOPPED" else STATUS[code]
        notify({"Robot": ROBOT, "Status": status, "Exit code": code, **facts, "Run folder": str(rd)}, log, dry_run)
    return code


def demo(tmp):
    """A bug while a closer also fails, an ops STOP, the re-run with a business exception, a clean end, a 2nd copy."""
    closed, handled, cards, reports, shut = [], [], [], [], ["evidence", "core", "excel", "browser"]
    fail = {"T2": BusinessError("over limit for Tan Ah Kow", code="OVER_LIMIT"), "T3": TypeError("98,765.43 + None")}
    cp, log = Checkpoint(tmp / "checkpoint.json"), get_logger(tmp / "run.log.jsonl", name="shutdown", console=False)

    def opener(stack, rd, log):                                          # open_apps with fakes that record closing
        for name in ("browser", "excel", "core"):
            enter(stack, contextlib.ExitStack(), name, log).callback(closed.append, name)
        stack.callback(quietly, (rd / "core.pid").unlink, "core pid file", log)   # a closer that fails (no file)
        stack.push(on_error(lambda: closed.append("evidence"), log))

    def handle(apps, item):
        if item in fail:
            raise fail[item]
        handled.append(item)
        if item == "T3":
            (tmp / "STOP.txt").touch()                                   # ops save STOP from Notepad while T3 runs

    def run():
        closed.clear()
        return run_robot(tmp, ["T1", "T2", "T3", "T4"], handle, lambda d, f: reports.append(list(f["item"])), log,
                         cp=cp, opener=opener, dry_run=True, notify=lambda *a: cards.append(str(notify_owner(*a))))

    assert run() == 5 and closed == shut and handled == ["T1"] and "NEEDS A FIX" in cards[0]   # not 3: failed close
    del fail["T3"]                                                       # bug fixed; ops stop the re-run after T3
    assert run() == 3 and closed == shut and handled == ["T1", "T3"] and "STOPPED" in cards[1] and reports == []
    (tmp / "STOP.txt").unlink()                                          # ops remove it: T2 fails again, T4 runs
    assert run() == 2 and closed == shut[1:] and handled[-1] == "T4" and reports == [["T2"]] and "BUSINESS" in cards[2]
    fail.clear()                                                         # the owner fixed T2: a clean end, no card
    assert run() == 0 and handled[-1] == "T2" and reports[-1] == [] and len(cards) == 3
    with single_instance(ROBOT, lock_dir=tmp):                           # the lock is free again; hold it
        assert run() == 6 and closed == [] and len(cards) == 3           # a second copy opens and sends nothing
    assert [exit_code(x) for x in (BusinessError("x"), OSError("x"), TypeError("x"))] == [2, 3, 5]
    text = (tmp / "run.log.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "CLOSE_FAILED" in text and '"TypeError"' in text and '"STOPPED"' in text
    assert not any(s in t for t in [text, *cards] for s in ("Tan Ah Kow", "98,765"))   # ids, never data
decisions: One contextlib.ExitStack per run. Each closer is registered the moment its app opens, so if the third app fails to start the first two still close, last opened first. The single_instance lock is entered first, so it is released last: a second copy cannot start while this run's apps are still closing. run_robot takes the lock itself, so it replaces the template's single_instance block in main(); keeping both makes every run exit 6.

Evidence first: the screenshot hook is pushed after the desktop app opens, so on an error or a STOP it runs before the app is killed. Browser takes its own screenshot on an error exit. No screenshot on a clean end. Each run writes under its own time stamp, so a re-run never overwrites the last failure's evidence.

Exit codes as the template: BusinessError 2, retryable (SystemError_, OSError) 3, anything else 5, second copy 6. Item failures give 3 if any is retryable, else 2. No card for 0 or 6. Every closer runs through quietly(): a failed close is logged and swallowed, else ExitStack replaces the real error with the close error and a bug (exit 5) shows up as an OSError (exit 3).

Kill switch: a file named STOP or STOP.txt (Notepad adds .txt) in the run folder, checked before any app opens and then before each item, never inside one. It raises SystemError_ STOPPED, so it takes the same shutdown path and exits 3: a re-run resumes from the checkpoint, and items that failed before the stop are not in it, so they are tried and reported again. The robot never deletes the file; ops do.

feature_flag('robot_enabled') also stops the robot, but a running process cannot see a changed env var or config, so it stops the next run. Only a graceful stop runs the closers: taskkill /F or a reboot runs none (the OS still frees the lock), so ops use the STOP file, not End task.
governance: The owner's Teams card carries robot, status, exit code, error code, counts and run folder, never the error message (it can hold a value). It is sent once, not retried, only printed in a dry run, and a failed send never changes the exit code. The webhook URL is a secret (anyone holding it can post): get_secret, never config.

The log line carries code, type, where and the ids in context, not the message or the traceback. process_all gets no log= because its lines repeat error messages; item failures go to report(done, failures), the robot's exceptions report, written before the lock is released. A run that ends early writes none: its failed items are not in the checkpoint, so the re-run reports them.

Kill only an app the robot started (app_connect(exe=...)): an app attached by its title can be a person's session. Screenshots can show customer data: they stay in the run folder under the retention rule.

import time
from contextlib import suppress
from functools import partial

import pandas as pd

from toolbank import RETRY_PROFILES, BusinessError, Checkpoint, SystemError_, act, api_get, attempt, process_all


def unconfirmed(ref):
    """The error for a send that may have arrived but does not show in the target system."""
    return SystemError_("sent but not confirmed: check the target system before it is sent again",
                        code="SUBMIT_UNCONFIRMED", ref=ref)


def release(held, ref):
    """Take ref off the hold list."""
    held.discard(ref)


def submit_once(ref, send, lookup, done, held, *, prepare=None, dry_run=False, log=print,
                sleep=time.sleep, clock=time.monotonic):
    """Send one item once (done, held: Checkpoint); returns 'skipped', 'already there', 'dry run' or 'submitted'."""
    if pd.isna(ref) or not str(ref).strip():
        raise BusinessError("no business reference: cannot check whether it was sent", code="MISSING_REF")
    ref = str(ref).strip()
    if done.is_done(ref):
        return "skipped"                                  # confirmed earlier for this business date
    if lookup(ref):                                       # an error here stops the item: never send blind
        if not dry_run:
            done.mark_done(ref)
            release(held, ref)                            # a held send that arrived after all
        return "already there"
    if held.is_done(ref):
        raise unconfirmed(ref)                            # a send started earlier and never showed: a person checks
    if prepare is not None:                               # open and fill the form: safe to repeat
        attempt(prepare, name=f"prepare {ref}", log=log, sleep=sleep, clock=clock, **RETRY_PROFILES["ui"])
    if not dry_run:
        held.mark_done(ref)                               # before the send: a timeout, crash or Ctrl+C leaves it held
    sent = []
    there = lambda: bool(sent) and lookup(ref)            # look again only once something may have been sent

    def go():
        if sent:                                          # try 2 only looks: the lookup said no, so never resend
            raise unconfirmed(ref)
        sent.append(ref)
        return act(send, dry_run=dry_run, log=lambda m: log(f"submit {ref}: {m}"))

    try:
        attempt(go, verify=None if dry_run else there, already_done=there, name=f"submit {ref}", log=log,
                poll_s=5.0, sleep=sleep, clock=clock, **dict(RETRY_PROFILES["submit"], tries=2))
    except BusinessError:
        release(held, ref)                                # the target said no: nothing to hold
        raise
    except SystemError_ as e:
        raise unconfirmed(ref) from e
    if dry_run:
        return "dry run"
    done.mark_done(ref)                                   # at once: a crash after this line cannot resend
    release(held, ref)
    return "submitted"


def rest_lookup(session, url, field="reference"):
    """lookup(ref) for a REST target: True only if a returned record carries ref exactly; 404 = not there."""
    def lookup(ref):
        try:
            rows = api_get(session, url, params={field: ref}) or []      # adapt if the API wraps its list
        except BusinessError as e:
            if e.context.get("status") != 404:
                raise                                     # 400 etc.: the reference itself is wrong
            return False
        return any(str(r.get(field, "")).strip() == str(ref).strip() for r in rows)   # not "the search found rows"
    return lookup


class FakeTime:
    """For the demo: sleeping only moves this clock, so waits take no real time."""
    now = 0.0
    def clock(self): return self.now
    def sleep(self, s): self.now += s


class FakePortal:
    """Demo target. first: 'timeout' (item kept, reply lost), 'lost' (both), 'crash' (Ctrl+C mid-send), 'reject' (400)."""
    def __init__(self, first="ok"): self.first, self.received, self.sends = first, [], 0
    def lookup(self, ref): return ref in self.received

    def send(self, ref):
        self.sends += 1
        mode = self.first if self.sends == 1 else "ok"
        if mode == "reject": raise BusinessError("HTTP 400: rejected", code="HTTP_400")
        if mode == "crash": raise KeyboardInterrupt
        if mode != "lost": self.received.append(ref)
        if mode in ("timeout", "lost"): raise TimeoutError("no reply within 60 s")
        return f"CONF-{ref}"


def demo(tmp):
    """Reply lost: one send, skipped on a re-run. Both lost or Ctrl+C mid-send: held, never resent, cleared once found."""
    t, log = FakeTime(), []
    kw = dict(log=log.append, sleep=t.sleep, clock=t.clock)
    done, held = Checkpoint(tmp / "submitted.json"), Checkpoint(tmp / "unconfirmed.json")
    p = FakePortal(first="timeout")
    send = partial(p.send, "PAY-1")
    assert submit_once("PAY-1", send, p.lookup, done, held, dry_run=True, **kw) == "dry run"
    assert p.sends == 0 and not held.is_done("PAY-1") and log[-1].startswith("submit PAY-1: [dry-run] would call send(")
    assert submit_once(" PAY-1 ", send, p.lookup, done, held, **kw) == "submitted" and not held.is_done("PAY-1")
    assert submit_once("PAY-1", send, p.lookup, Checkpoint(tmp / "submitted.json"), held, **kw) == "skipped"

    def run(portal, ref):                                 # one robot run over one item -> the failures table
        handler = lambda item: submit_once(item["ref"], partial(portal.send, item["ref"]), portal.lookup, done, held, **kw)
        return process_all([{"ref": ref}], handler, key=lambda item: item["ref"])[1]
    lost, killed = FakePortal(first="lost"), FakePortal(first="crash")
    with suppress(KeyboardInterrupt):                     # the robot is stopped mid-send
        run(killed, "PAY-3")
    for _ in range(2):                                    # the run, then a re-run: never a second send
        assert run(lost, "PAY-2").loc[0, "code"] == run(killed, "PAY-3").loc[0, "code"] == "SUBMIT_UNCONFIRMED"
    assert p.sends == lost.sends == killed.sends == 1 and held.is_done("PAY-2") and not done.is_done("PAY-2")
    killed.received.append("PAY-3")                       # the portal shows it after all: the hold clears itself
    assert run(killed, "PAY-3").empty and done.is_done("PAY-3") and not held.is_done("PAY-3")
    assert run(FakePortal(first="reject"), "PAY-4").loc[0, "code"] == "HTTP_400" and not held.is_done("PAY-4")
    assert run(FakePortal(), " ").loc[0, "code"] == "MISSING_REF"
decisions: Key every item by its business reference (payment id, instruction ref), trimmed, never a row number: rows move when a file is re-sorted, a reference does not. A blank one is BusinessError MISSING_REF. Key process_all(checkpoint=...) by the same trimmed reference, so one repeated in the input is reported (DUPLICATE_KEY), not returned as 'skipped'.

Look the reference up before the send, outside attempt (attempt reads an error in already_done as 'not there'). lookup(ref) raises when it cannot search and is True only for an exact match: rest_lookup compares trimmed text, case counts (a wrong 'found' would drop a payment silently, a wrong 'not found' only holds it), 404 is not there, other 4xx is BusinessError.

prepare() (open the form, fill it) runs first as its own screen step (RETRY_PROFILES['ui'], up to 3 tries). send() (press Submit, POST) is the point of no return: RETRY_PROFILES['submit'] with tries raised to 2 only because already_done is given, and the second try never sends, it looks the reference up 2 s after a failed send.

Confirmed means the lookup finds the reference within 30 s, polled every 5 s (it is a search, not a screen check), not that send() returned. The checkpoint (its own file, submitted.json) is marked right after, so later steps of the item can fail and re-run without a resend.

The reference goes on the hold list (unconfirmed.json) just before send() and comes off when the lookup finds it. Anything else after that point (a timeout, a slow back-end, a crash, Ctrl+C, a 401) leaves it held, never checkpointed: SystemError_ SUBMIT_UNCONFIRMED (at once, or at the next run after a crash), and every later run raises it again without sending.

A refusal (BusinessError from send(), e.g. HTTP 400) is a definite 'not sent': off the hold list, recorded as a business exception, not retried in this run. Raise BusinessError in send() only when the target said no.

process_all stops after 3 system failures in a row, so an outage leaves at most 3 references on hold, not the whole batch. Until they are found or cleared, a re-run that meets them in a row stops there again.
governance: The robot takes a reference off unconfirmed.json only when the lookup finds it or the target refuses it. Any other removal is a person's, after checking the target system: that edit is the approval to send it again.

Keep unconfirmed.json outside the dated run folder (e.g. work/<robot>/unconfirmed.json) so a hold survives into the next business date. The checkpoint covers one business date; the lookup in the target system is the guard across days and machines.
For an API use http_session() (it never resends a POST) and send the reference as an idempotency key if the API accepts one.

This block's own errors carry the reference only. attempt's log lines and a refusal carry the target's error text (an HTTP 400 or 503 body), which can echo names or amounts that get_logger does not mask: in send(), catch it and raise your own error with a short code.

Rehearse with dry_run=True before the first live run: it runs the lookup and prepare(), logs each send through act instead of making it and writes neither file; the returned status shows what is already there. If the target saves drafts, skip prepare() in a dry run.

import os
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from toolbank import RETRY_PROFILES, RobotError, SystemError_, attempt, get_secret

SEL = {"user": "#username", "password": "#password", "submit": "button[type=submit]",   # change per portal
       "home": "#logout", "message": ".login-error", "logout": "#logout"}       # home: only a logged-in page has it
LOGIN_MESSAGES = [("locked", "AUTH", "locked"), ("too many", "AUTH", "locked"), ("expired", "AUTH", "expired password"),
                  ("invalid", "AUTH", "invalid credentials"), ("incorrect", "AUTH", "invalid credentials"),
                  ("maintenance", "SYSTEM", "maintenance"), ("unavailable", "SYSTEM", "unavailable")]  # word, kind, reason


def message(b):
    """The login page's message in lower case; '' when it shows none (never ms=0: Playwright reads it as no limit)."""
    return b.text(SEL["message"]).strip().lower() if b.exists(SEL["message"], ms=200) else ""


def login_state(b, before=""):
    """('OK', '') on the home page, (kind, reason) for a new message on the login page, None while it loads."""
    if b.exists(SEL["home"], ms=200):                     # home first: a banner there ("expires in 5 days") is fine
        return "OK", ""
    text = message(b)
    if not text or text == before:                        # nothing yet, or what the page showed before the submit
        return None
    return next(((kind, why) for word, kind, why in LOGIN_MESSAGES if word in text), ("AUTH", "unrecognised message"))


def login(b, user, password, *, log=print, sleep=time.sleep, clock=time.monotonic):
    """One try on the open login page: submit, wait up to 30 s for the home page or a new message, act on it."""
    before, seen = message(b), {}
    def answered():                                       # remember what the page said: a toast can fade
        seen["state"] = login_state(b, before)
        return seen["state"]
    try:
        attempt(lambda: b.login(user, password, SEL["user"], SEL["password"], SEL["submit"]), verify=answered,
                name="login", log=lambda m: log(m.replace(password, "***")), sleep=sleep, clock=clock,
                **RETRY_PROFILES["login"])
    except SystemError_:
        raise SystemError_("login did not finish (slow page or no form): re-run later", code="LOGIN_TIMEOUT") from None
    kind, reason = seen["state"]
    if kind == "AUTH":
        raise RobotError(f"login refused ({reason}): stop and tell the robot owner", code="AUTH", reason=reason)
    if kind == "SYSTEM":
        raise SystemError_(f"login page says {reason}: re-run later", code="LOGIN_UNAVAILABLE", reason=reason)
    log("login: ok")


@contextmanager
def portal_session(b, url, session_file, user_secret, password_secret, *, max_age_h=8, keep=False, log=print,
                   sleep=time.sleep, clock=time.monotonic):
    """`with portal_session(b, ...):` reuse a young saved session or log in once; at the end log out, delete it."""
    f = Path(session_file)
    fresh = f.exists() and time.time() - f.stat().st_mtime < max_age_h * 3600
    if fresh:
        b.load_session(f)
    b.goto(url)
    if fresh and b.exists(SEL["home"], ms=5000):
        log("login: saved session reused")
    else:
        f.unlink(missing_ok=True)                         # too old or refused by the portal: never reuse it
        try:
            user, password = get_secret(user_secret), get_secret(password_secret)   # env var or Credential Manager
        except KeyError as e:
            raise RobotError(e.args[0], code="NO_SECRET") from e                 # a setup error, not bad data
        login(b, user, password, log=log, sleep=sleep, clock=clock)
        f.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)   # mode: only when the folder is new
        b.save_session(f)
        f.chmod(0o600)                                    # owner only on Linux; on Windows the folder's ACL decides
    try:
        yield b
    finally:
        if not keep:
            try:
                b.click(SEL["logout"])
            except Exception as e:                        # page gone or session over: still delete the file
                log(f"logout failed: {type(e).__name__}")
            f.unlink(missing_ok=True)


class FakeTime:
    """For the demo: sleeping only moves this clock, so waits take no real time."""
    now = 0.0
    def clock(self): return self.now
    def sleep(self, s): self.now += s


class FakeBrowser:
    """For the demo: Browser's methods used above; shown: the page's message, reply: a wrong password's (None: none)."""
    page, cookie, tries = "", "", 0
    def __init__(self, server, password, reply="Invalid user ID or password", shown=""):
        self.server, self.password, self.reply, self.shown = server, password, reply, shown
    def goto(self, url): self.page = "home" if self.cookie in self.server else "login"
    def exists(self, sel, ms=2000): return self.page == "home" if sel == SEL["home"] else bool(self.shown)
    def text(self, sel): return self.shown
    def click(self, sel): self.server.discard(self.cookie); self.page = "login"     # the logout link
    def save_session(self, path): Path(path).write_text(self.cookie)
    def load_session(self, path): self.cookie = Path(path).read_text()
    def login(self, user, password, *selectors):
        self.tries += 1
        if password == self.password: self.cookie, self.page = user, "home"; self.server.add(user)
        elif self.reply: self.shown = self.reply


def demo(tmp):
    """Wrong password: AUTH after one try. Good one: logged in, the next run reuses the session, logout deletes it.
    A page that never answers, showing an old message: LOGIN_TIMEOUT after 30 s, not AUTH. No password logged."""
    t, log, server, url = FakeTime(), [], set(), "https://portal.example/"
    kw = dict(log=log.append, sleep=t.sleep, clock=t.clock)
    names, session = ("DEMO_PORTAL_USER", "DEMO_PORTAL_PASSWORD"), tmp / "secure" / "portal_session.json"
    def refusal(browser):
        try:
            with portal_session(browser, url, session, *names, **kw): pass
        except RobotError as e:
            return e
        raise AssertionError("expected the login to be refused")
    with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {names[0]: "robot01", names[1]: "Wr0ng-pass"}):   # restored afterwards
        b = FakeBrowser(server, password="Right-pass")
        e = refusal(b)
        assert e.code == "AUTH" and e.context == {"reason": "invalid credentials"} and b.tries == 1
        os.environ[names[1]] = "Right-pass"
        with portal_session(b, url, session, *names, keep=True, **kw):
            assert b.page == "home" and b.tries == 2 and session.exists()
        nxt = FakeBrowser(server, password="Right-pass")    # the next run: no login
        with portal_session(nxt, url, session, *names, **kw):
            assert nxt.page == "home" and nxt.tries == 0
        assert not session.exists() and not server           # logged out, file deleted
        stale = FakeBrowser(server, password="other", reply=None, shown="Your session has expired")
        assert refusal(stale).code == "LOGIN_TIMEOUT" and stale.tries == 1 and t.now == 30
        assert not any("Right-pass" in m or "Wr0ng-pass" in m for m in log)
decisions: One try only (RETRY_PROFILES['login']): every wrong password counts towards the lockout limit (often 3 to 5), and a locked service account stops every robot that uses it.

After submit, wait up to 30 s for the home page or a new message: one the page showed before the submit ('your session has expired' after a refused saved session) is not the answer. Neither is SystemError_ LOGIN_TIMEOUT (slow page, no form): the template exits 3, safe to re-run later at the cost of one more try.

A message with locked, too many, expired, invalid or incorrect is RobotError AUTH: the run stops (template exit 5) and the owner fixes the account first. An unknown message is AUTH too, since guessing could lock the account: add the portal's words to LOGIN_MESSAGES. 'maintenance' or 'unavailable' is SystemError_ LOGIN_UNAVAILABLE: the portal is down, re-run later.
Reuse a saved session younger than 8 hours (one working day) only if the home page shows within 5 s; otherwise delete the file and log in.
A missing secret is RobotError NO_SECRET (exit 5, fix the setup), not the KeyError get_secret raises, which classify would report as bad data (exit 2).
governance: Credentials come from get_secret (env var, or Windows Credential Manager through keyring) only when a login is needed and are never logged: attempt's log lines go through a password mask, errors carry a reason word, never the screen text (it can name the user).

The session file is a password: owner-only (chmod 600, and a new folder 700, on Linux; on Windows the folder's ACL decides), in a folder only the robot account can read, not the run folder with reports, never a shared drive or git.
Logout in finally deletes the session file, so a failed run leaves no live session behind. keep=True (a robot that runs many times a day) is bounded by the 8-hour limit.

patterns.when: A robot that signs in to a web portal with a service account, once per run, around the PROCESS part.

decisions: In a finished run every item ends in one state: done (in the checkpoint), business exception or system failure, each failure a row in the report. A run that stops (SYSTEM_STREAK, a bug) leaves the rest for the re-run.

Checkpoint key = the business reference (payment id) trimmed and in capitals (ref_key), never the row number: a re-sorted or re-sent file still resumes right, and ' pay-1002' is the same payment as 'PAY-1002'. A blank or repeated reference is reported as MISSING_KEY / DUPLICATE_KEY, never skipped silently.
Wrong data raises BusinessError with a short code the owner can act on (MISSING_ACCOUNT, BAD_AMOUNT, NOT_IN_LEDGER, AMOUNT_MISMATCH): recorded, never retried, the loop goes on.

A failing environment raises SystemError_ with its own code (LEDGER_DOWN) or is a plain OSError / TimeoutError, which process_all treats the same: recorded as retryable and left for the re-run, not retried in this run. If a read must succeed in the same run, wrap it in attempt with RETRY_PROFILES['read'] inside the handler.

The re-run retries every failure, also a post that went through before its reply timed out. A handler that posts or pays must look the reference up before it sends (attempt with already_done=, the submit-once block); check_payment only reads.

Stop after 3 system failures in a row (max_consecutive_system=3): one or two blips do not stop a long queue, and a system that is down stops the run after 3 items instead of timing out on every one. A success or a business exception resets the count, so a system that fails every other item never trips it: watch the retryable count.

A bug (TypeError, AttributeError) stops the run at once (exit 5): every item would fail the same way. A KeyError or ValueError counts as bad data (BAD_DATA), so check the fields you need and raise your own code: check_payment turns every error of converting the amount (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError for an infinite one) into BAD_AMOUNT.
Exit code from the failures: 3 if any is retryable (re-run, the checkpoint skips what is done), else 2 if any (send the report), else 0.

The report is deleted at the start and written at the end of every run (safe_write_excel: temp file and rename). After the last re-run it lists exactly the items still open; a clean run writes an empty one, so 'no exceptions' is on file. A run stopped by SYSTEM_STREAK (exit 3) or by a bug (exit 5) leaves no report: the log says why.
progress() logs every 100 items (count, %, rate, time left): 50 lines for a 5,000 item queue, enough to spot a slowdown.
Money is compared in cents (cents), never as floats.
governance: Logs and the report carry the reference and the code, never values: write 'amount differs from the ledger', not the two amounts. process_all logs each failure message (log=log.warning); get_logger masks account-like numbers as a second line of defence.

A library error message can hold a value (could not convert string to float: '1,234 USD'): catch it where you convert and raise your own BusinessError without the value, as check_payment does for the amount.
ACTIONS (code -> what the owner does next) is part of the exception table the process owner signs in design: a new code needs their sign-off.
The checkpoint holds references only. Keep it in the dated run folder (run_dir) with the log, under the same retention rule; delete it only to process a business date again on purpose.

import os
import time
import zipfile
from datetime import date, datetime

import pandas as pd

from toolbank import (RETRY_PROFILES, BusinessError, MissingColumns, SystemError_, archive, assert_totals_match,
                      assert_unique, attempt, check_schema, cleanse, control_totals, file_sha256, is_locked, read_any,
                      standard_columns, to_date, to_number, wait_for_file)

ALIASES = {"ref": ["Reference", "Txn Ref", "Payment Ref"], "account": ["Account No", "Acct No", "Account Number"],
           "amount": ["Amt", "Amount (SGD)"], "value_date": ["Val Dt", "Value Dt"]}    # signed off by the owner
SCHEMA = {"ref": "text", "account": "text", "amount": "number", "value_date": "date"}


def wait_for_input(pattern, day=None, timeout_s=3600, stable_s=30, poll_s=10, locked=is_locked, log=print,
                   sleep=time.sleep):
    """The file of business date `day` (a date, today if None) once complete and closed; else SystemError_ (exit 3)."""
    since = datetime.combine(day or date.today(), datetime.min.time())
    path = wait_for_file(pattern, timeout_s=timeout_s, poll_s=poll_s, stable_s=stable_s, min_mtime=since)

    def closed():
        if locked(path):
            raise SystemError_("the input is open in another program", code="FILE_LOCKED", file=path.name)

    attempt(closed, name=f"open {path.name}", log=log, sleep=sleep, **RETRY_PROFILES["file_lock"])
    return path


def load_input(path, expected=None):
    """Read and check the whole file: (df, evidence), or BusinessError with a code for the owner (exit 2).
    expected: the sender's control totals, e.g. {"rows": 2, "sum": 950.5} from the trailer."""
    sha = file_sha256(path)                               # before the read: the evidence names the bytes used
    reject = lambda why, code, **ids: BusinessError(why, code=code, file=path.name, **ids)
    try:
        df = standard_columns(read_any(path, dtype=str), ALIASES)      # text: '00123' keeps its zeros
    except MissingColumns as e:                           # two columns for one name: 'Amount' and 'Amt'
        raise reject(str(e), "MISSING_COLUMNS") from None
    except (ValueError, zipfile.BadZipFile) as e:          # no header, unknown type, broken or protected workbook
        raise reject(str(e), "UNREADABLE") from None
    if missing := [c for c in SCHEMA if c not in df.columns]:     # not the headers found: they may be data
        raise reject(f"missing columns {missing}", "MISSING_COLUMNS")
    df = cleanse(df).dropna(how="all")                    # ',,,' is no row
    if df.empty:
        raise reject("the file has a header but no rows", "EMPTY_INPUT")
    df["amount"], df["value_date"] = to_number(df["amount"]), to_date(df["value_date"])
    bad = df["ref"].isna() | df["amount"].isna() | df["value_date"].isna()
    if bad.any():                                         # unparsable -> NaN, which check_schema cannot see
        raise reject(f"{int(bad.sum())} rows with a blank ref, amount or date, or one that does not parse",
                     "BAD_VALUES", rows=[int(i) + 2 for i in df.index[bad][:10]])
    try:
        assert_unique(df.assign(ref=df["ref"].str.upper()), "ref")     # 'pay-1' and 'PAY-1' are one reference
    except ValueError as e:
        raise reject(str(e), "DUPLICATE_KEY") from None
    if problems := check_schema(df, SCHEMA):
        raise reject("; ".join(problems), "WRONG_TYPES")
    totals = control_totals(df, "amount", key_col="ref")
    try:
        assert_totals_match(expected or {}, totals)
    except ValueError as e:
        raise reject(f"differs from the sender's control totals: {e}", "TOTALS_MISMATCH") from None
    return df, {"file": path.name, "bytes": path.stat().st_size, "sha256": sha, **totals}


def archive_if_final(path, evidence, exit_code, archive_dir):
    """After the run: archive the input when every item is final (exit 0 or 2) and the file is unchanged."""
    if exit_code not in (0, 2):
        return None                                       # exit 3: the re-run needs the file where it is
    if file_sha256(path) != evidence["sha256"]:
        raise BusinessError("the input changed during the run: not archived", code="INPUT_CHANGED", file=path.name)
    target = archive(path, archive_dir)
    if path.exists():                                     # archive() keeps the day's first file of this name
        raise BusinessError("a file of this name is already archived today", code="ARCHIVE_EXISTS", file=path.name)
    return target


def demo(tmp):
    """Today's file is taken, yesterday's is not; other headers give the same totals; a file kept open gives up
    after 150 s; empty, headerless, unreadable, duplicate and bad files are rejected by code; archive when final."""
    def expect(code, fn, *args, **kw):
        try:
            fn(*args, **kw)
        except (BusinessError, SystemError_) as e:
            assert e.code == code and "00123456" not in str(e), f"{code} without data expected, got {e}"
        else:
            raise AssertionError(f"{code} expected")

    head = "Reference,Account No,Amount,Value Date\n"
    rows = 'PAY-1,00123456,"1,250.50",12/11/2026\nPAY-2,00987654,(300.00),13/11/2026\n,,,\n'   # a blank row too
    for folder in ("inbox", "old"):
        (tmp / folder).mkdir()
        (tmp / folder / "payments.csv").write_text(head + rows)
    since = datetime.combine(date.today(), datetime.min.time()).timestamp()
    os.utime(tmp / "old" / "payments.csv", (since - 3600, since - 3600))     # last saved yesterday evening
    expect("FILE_TIMEOUT", wait_for_input, tmp / "old" / "*.csv", stable_s=0, poll_s=0, timeout_s=0.01)
    waits, log = [], []                                   # fake sleep: records the waits, takes no time
    expect("STEP_FAILED", wait_for_input, tmp / "inbox" / "*.csv", stable_s=0, poll_s=0, timeout_s=1,
           locked=lambda p: True, log=log.append, sleep=waits.append)
    assert waits == [10, 20, 40, 80] and len(log) == 5    # 5 tries, 150 s in all

    path = wait_for_input(tmp / "inbox" / "*.csv", stable_s=0, poll_s=0, timeout_s=1)
    df, ev = load_input(path, expected={"rows": 2, "sum": 950.5})
    assert (ev["rows"], ev["sum"], df.loc[0, "account"]) == (2, 950.5, "00123456")
    expect("TOTALS_MISMATCH", load_input, path, expected={"rows": 3})
    renamed = tmp / "renamed.xlsx"                        # the same data from another export, other headers
    pd.DataFrame({"Txn Ref": ["PAY-1", "PAY-2"], "Acct No": ["00123456", "00987654"], "Amt": [1250.5, -300],
                  "Val Dt": pd.to_datetime(["2026-11-12", "2026-11-13"])}).to_excel(renamed, index=False)
    ev2 = load_input(renamed)[1]
    assert all(ev2[k] == ev[k] for k in ("rows", "sum", "abs_sum", "distinct_keys"))

    bad = {"EMPTY_INPUT.csv": head + ",,,\n", "DUPLICATE_KEY.csv": head + rows + "pay-1 ,00555555,5,12/11/2026\n",
           "MISSING_COLUMNS.csv": rows, "UNREADABLE.pdf": "%PDF-1.7",              # no header row at all
           "BAD_VALUES.csv": head + "PAY-1,00123456,five,12/11/2026\n,00123456,5,12/11/2026\n,00987654,5,12/11/2026\n",
           "UNREADABLE.xlsx": head + rows}                # a CSV saved under an .xlsx name
    for name, text in bad.items():
        (tmp / name).write_text(text)
        expect(name.split(".")[0], load_input, tmp / name)

    assert archive_if_final(path, ev, 3, tmp / "archive") is None and path.exists()
    assert file_sha256(archive_if_final(path, ev, 0, tmp / "archive")) == ev["sha256"] and not path.exists()
    path.write_text(head + rows)                          # the same name delivered again the same day
    expect("ARCHIVE_EXISTS", archive_if_final, path, load_input(path)[1], 0, tmp / "archive")
    renamed.write_bytes(renamed.read_bytes() + b"\0")    # someone saves over the input during the run
    expect("INPUT_CHANGED", archive_if_final, renamed, ev2, 0, tmp / "archive")
    assert path.exists() and renamed.exists()
decisions: The business date's file only: wait_for_file with min_mtime = midnight of that date, so yesterday's file left in the folder is never taken again. No file within 1 h (timeout_s=3600) is SystemError_ FILE_TIMEOUT: exit 3, re-run or chase the sender. One file per run: if two match, the newest is taken; for several files a day use watch_folder.

Complete: the size must stay the same for 30 s (stable_s=30, checked every 10 s); a 0-byte file never counts as arrived. Closed: is_locked checked 5 times, 10 s apart and doubling (RETRY_PROFILES['file_lock'], 150 s in all), then SystemError_ STEP_FAILED, exit 3. is_locked opens the file for append, so the robot account needs modify rights on the inbox (archive needs them too).
Read every column as text (dtype=str), then convert only the amount and the value date (to_number, to_date): account numbers keep their leading zeros and long references do not turn into floats.

Header variants go through ALIASES (standard_columns, which also forgives case, spaces and punctuation: 'VALUE_DATE'); then all four standard names must be there. read_any(required=) alone would reject another name ('Val Dt'), so it is not used here.

Reject the whole file with a BusinessError and a code (exit 2, tell the owner): MISSING_COLUMNS (also two columns for one name), UNREADABLE (no header, an unknown file type, a broken or password-protected workbook), EMPTY_INPUT (no rows once wholly blank rows such as ',,,' are dropped), BAD_VALUES (a blank ref, or an amount or date that is blank or does not parse), DUPLICATE_KEY (assert_unique on ref trimmed and in capitals, checked after BAD_VALUES so two blank refs are not called duplicates), WRONG_TYPES, TOTALS_MISMATCH. One bad row usually means the export changed; processing the rest would hide that. A broken workbook raises zipfile.BadZipFile, which the template would call a bug (exit 5), so it is caught as UNREADABLE.

check_schema is the last guard that the frame has the types the next steps assume. It cannot see a value that did not parse (to_number makes it NaN), so those are counted first and named by row number (header on row 1; empty lines of a CSV are not counted).

Archive only when every item reached a final state (exit 0 or 2) and the SHA-256 is unchanged; on exit 3 the file stays for the re-run. A rejected file has no evidence, so it is never archived: it stays in the inbox for the owner to replace.
governance: Evidence for every accepted file before any item is processed: name, size, SHA-256 and control totals (rows, sum, absolute sum, distinct refs); log it with extra=. The hash is taken before the read, so it names the bytes the robot used.

If the sender gives a count and total (trailer row, control file, cover email), pass them as expected= with the keys rows and sum (abs_sum, distinct_keys also work; assert_totals_match ignores any other key): a difference is TOTALS_MISMATCH and nothing is processed.

Rejection messages carry codes, column names, references and row numbers, never an item's amount or an account number; the owner opens the file to see the values. MISSING_COLUMNS names only the missing standard names, not the headers found: in a file without a header row those are the first row's values. TOTALS_MISMATCH shows the file totals, which the evidence holds anyway.
ALIASES is configuration the process owner signs off: a new header spelling is a reviewed change, not a quiet code fix.

The archive keeps the file as YYYYMMDD_name, the input evidence for audit, under the bank's retention rule. archive() keeps the day's first file of a name, so a second one stays in the inbox as ARCHIVE_EXISTS for a person to check.

import os
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from toolbank import (BusinessError, col_letter, highlight_cells, normalise_currency, normalise_key, recon_summary,
                      reconcile, to_date, to_number, write_report)

TOL_CENTS = 1                                             # amounts this many cents apart still match; 0 for cash
WIDTH = 10                                                # refs are zero-padded to this many characters
COMPARE = ["amount", "ccy", "value_date"]
STATUSES = ["MATCHED", "BREAK", "LEFT_ONLY", "RIGHT_ONLY"]
BREAK_VIEW = ["key", "break_cols", "amount_l", "amount_r", "amount_diff", "ccy_l", "ccy_r", "value_date_l",
              "value_date_r", "row_l", "row_r"]
FORMATS = {"amount_l": "#,##0.00", "amount_r": "#,##0.00", "amount_diff": "#,##0.00",
           "value_date_l": "dd-mmm-yyyy", "value_date_r": "dd-mmm-yyyy"}


def normalise(df, side, ref, amount, ccy, value_date):
    """One side -> key, amount, ccy, value_date, row; stops on blank or unreadable values or duplicate refs."""
    refs = df[ref].astype("Int64") if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[ref]) else df[ref]   # 123.0 -> 123
    key, row = normalise_key(refs), pd.Series(df.index + 2, index=df.index)
    out = pd.DataFrame({"key": key.str.zfill(WIDTH).where(key.fillna("") != "", f"NOREF-{side}-" + row.astype(str)),
                        "amount": to_number(df[amount]), "ccy": normalise_currency(df[ccy]).replace("", pd.NA),
                        "value_date": to_date(df[value_date]).dt.normalize(), "row": row})
    bad = out[COMPARE].isna().any(axis=1)
    if bad.any():
        raise BusinessError(f"{side}: blank or unreadable amount, currency or date", code="UNREADABLE", side=side,
                            rows=out.loc[bad, "row"].tolist()[:20])
    dup = out["key"].duplicated(keep=False)
    if dup.any():
        raise BusinessError(f"{side}: a ref is on more than one row", code="DUPLICATE_KEYS", side=side,
                            refs=sorted(set(out.loc[dup, "key"]))[:20])
    return out


def summary(recon, rows_left, rows_right, tol_cents):
    """Rows per status (zeros included), the matches that used the tolerance, and each side's row count."""
    counts = recon_summary(recon).set_index("status")["count"].reindex(STATUSES, fill_value=0)
    used = int(((recon["status"] == "MATCHED") & (recon["amount_diff"] != 0)).sum())
    extra = {f"MATCHED within {tol_cents} cent tolerance": used, "rows left": rows_left, "rows right": rows_right}
    return pd.DataFrame({"status": [*counts.index, *extra], "count": [*counts.astype(int), *extra.values()]})


def break_cells(breaks):
    """Excel addresses of the differing fields on the Breaks sheet (both sides), for highlight_cells."""
    letter = {c: col_letter(i) for i, c in enumerate(breaks.columns, start=1)}
    return [f"{letter[c + s]}{r}" for r, cols in enumerate(breaks["break_cols"], start=2)
            for c in cols.split(",") for s in ("_l", "_r")]


def write_recon_report(recon, summary_df, path):
    """Summary / Breaks / Left only / Right only with differing cells yellow; built under a temp name, then renamed."""
    path = Path(path)
    part = path.with_name(f"~{path.stem}.part.xlsx")
    of = lambda s: recon[recon["status"] == s].reset_index(drop=True)
    breaks = of("BREAK")[BREAK_VIEW]
    sheets = {"Summary": summary_df, "Breaks": breaks, "Left only": of("LEFT_ONLY").filter(regex="^key$|_l$"),
              "Right only": of("RIGHT_ONLY").filter(regex="^key$|_r$")}
    try:
        write_report(part, sheets, number_formats=FORMATS)
        highlight_cells(part, "Breaks", break_cells(breaks))
        os.replace(part, path)
    finally:
        part.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return path


def run_recon(left, left_cols, right, right_cols, path, tol_cents=TOL_CENTS, log=print):
    """Normalise both sides, reconcile, write the report; returns the recon frame (one row per ref, with status).
    left_cols / right_cols = the (ref, amount, ccy, value_date) column names of each side."""
    L, R = normalise(left, "L", *left_cols), normalise(right, "R", *right_cols)
    recon = reconcile(L, R, on="key", compare=COMPARE, tolerance={"amount": tol_cents / 100})
    write_recon_report(recon, summary(recon, len(L), len(R), tol_cents), path)
    log(f"recon {Path(path).name}: " + ", ".join(f"{s} {n}" for s, n in recon["status"].value_counts().items()))
    return recon


def exit_code(recon):
    """The template's exit code: 0 when every ref matched, 2 (send the report to the owner) when any did not."""
    return 2 if (recon["status"] != "MATCHED").any() else 0


def demo(tmp):
    """Case, space, zero-padding, currency-alias and 0.004 rounding differences match; real breaks are reported with
    their cells yellow. A ref on two rows after normalising, an unreadable amount or a blank currency stops the run
    with no report."""
    from openpyxl import load_workbook
    ledger = pd.DataFrame({"Ref": ["123", "ab-77", " 0045", "9001", "9002", "9003", ""],
                           "Amount": ["1,000.00", "250.50", "(75.00)", "500.00", "10.00", "20.00", "5.00"],
                           "Ccy": ["usd", "S$", "EUR", "USD", "USD", "USD", "SGD"], "Value Date": "06/03/2026"})
    bank = pd.DataFrame({"reference": ["0000000123", "AB77 ", "45", "9001", "9002", "9100"],
                         "amt": [1000.004, 250.5, -75.0, 505.0, 10.0, 7.5],
                         "currency": ["USD", "SGD", "eur", "USD", "USD", "USD"],
                         "date": ["2026-03-06", "6/3/2026", "2026-03-06", "2026-03-06", "2026-03-09", "2026-03-06"]})
    cols_l, cols_r, lines = ("Ref", "Amount", "Ccy", "Value Date"), ("reference", "amt", "currency", "date"), []
    recon = run_recon(ledger, cols_l, bank, cols_r, tmp / "recon.xlsx", log=lines.append)
    st = recon.set_index("key")["status"]
    assert exit_code(recon) == 2 and exit_code(recon[recon["status"] == "MATCHED"]) == 0
    assert set(st[st == "MATCHED"].index) == {"0000000123", "000000AB77", "0000000045"}
    assert st["0000009001"] == st["0000009002"] == "BREAK" and st["0000009100"] == "RIGHT_ONLY"
    assert st["0000009003"] == st["NOREF-L-8"] == "LEFT_ONLY" and "9001" not in lines[0]

    wb = load_workbook(tmp / "recon.xlsx")
    assert wb.sheetnames == ["Summary", "Breaks", "Left only", "Right only"]
    assert dict(wb["Summary"].iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True)) == {
        "MATCHED": 3, "BREAK": 2, "LEFT_ONLY": 2, "RIGHT_ONLY": 1, "MATCHED within 1 cent tolerance": 1,
        "rows left": 7, "rows right": 6}
    br = wb["Breaks"]                                     # row 2 = 9001 (amount differs), row 3 = 9002 (date)
    assert br["C2"].fill.fill_type == br["D2"].fill.fill_type == br["H3"].fill.fill_type == "solid"
    assert br["F2"].fill.fill_type is None and br["C3"].fill.fill_type is None

    duplicate = pd.concat([ledger, ledger[:1].assign(Ref="0123")], ignore_index=True)
    unreadable = ledger.replace({"Amount": {"500.00": "5OO.00"}, "Ccy": {"EUR": " "}})        # rows 5 and 4
    for bad, code, context in ((duplicate, "DUPLICATE_KEYS", {"refs": ["0000000123"]}),
                               (unreadable, "UNREADABLE", {"rows": [4, 5]})):
        try:
            run_recon(bad, cols_l, bank, cols_r, tmp / "stopped.xlsx", log=lines.append)
        except BusinessError as e:
            assert e.code == code and context.items() <= e.context.items() and not (tmp / "stopped.xlsx").exists()
        else:
            raise AssertionError(f"expected {code}")
decisions: Normalise both sides the same way before matching: normalise_key padded to 10 characters (' ab-77' = 'AB77 ', '45' = '0045'; a longer ref is kept whole), to_number ('(75.00)' = -75), to_date (day-first text, ISO, Excel serials), normalise_currency ('S$' = 'SGD').
A ref column read as numbers is made whole (Int64) first: normalise_key turns 123.0 into '1230'. Read refs of 16+ digits as text (dtype=str): Excel keeps only 15 digits of a number.

Amounts match within TOL_CENTS = 1 cent, set per recon: a 4-decimal source against a 2-decimal one (0.004 apart) matches, 0.02 apart is a break. 1 cent also hides a real 1-cent break, so the Summary counts the matches that used the tolerance. Use 0 for cash.
Currency and value date must be equal (the date without its time of day): a date one day off is a break, not a tolerance.
Duplicate refs on one side (after normalising) raise BusinessError DUPLICATE_KEYS and nothing is matched: which of the two rows pairs with the other side would be a guess.

A blank or unreadable amount, currency or date raises BusinessError UNREADABLE with the source rows (a currency of spaces is blank): reconcile counts blank against blank as equal, so two broken rows would match.
A blank ref does not stop the run: the row gets the key NOREF-L-<row> or NOREF-R-<row> and lands in Left only or Right only.

Breaks are a result, not an error: BREAK, LEFT_ONLY and RIGHT_ONLY rows go to the report, and exit_code returns 2 when there are any (the template's code for 'send the report to the owner'), 0 when every ref matched.
governance: Every row keeps its source row number (row_l, row_r = index + 2: the Excel row when the header is on row 1), so a reviewer can find it in the input file.
Summary lists all four statuses (zeros included) and each side's row count: matched + break + left only = rows left, and the same for the right.
Summary counts rows. It never adds amounts across currencies.
Differing cells are yellow on the Breaks sheet. Dates show as dd-mmm-yyyy (06-Mar-2026), which nobody reads as 3 June.
The report is built under a temporary name and renamed when complete, so nobody opens a half-written file. Nothing is written when the run stops.
The log line carries counts per status only; refs and amounts stay in the report.
The tolerance is a control setting: the Summary shows it, and a change goes through change control.
